evidence: Workbook Quality Checks!D8 requires real build work; Internal Quality Checks!D8 repeats it. The smallest compliant submission is a custom editing engine, isolated executable JS/HTML preview with recovery, and persistent revision library, not a static page or single CRUD screen: frozen task/instruction.md:1,3,5; environment/instructions/ui.md:3,5,7,9,11,15; behaviour.md:3,5,7,9; integration.md:7,9. A plausible weak submission is a polished static editor illustration with a canned running button and localStorage Save. It cannot satisfy tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23, which requires execution of freshly authored arithmetic/button code with two increasing outputs; nor gates/constraints/judge.toml:23,32, which require a real custom surface and exact saved source read through a separate clean context. A working textarea iframe playground also fails the explicitly public custom-surface rule, rather than receiving reward for a trivial wrapper. Both gate aggregations are all_pass (judge.toml:15); tests/scoring.toml:1-11 and tests/tools/score.py:40-48 make failed gates yield zero reward. Conforming alternative considered: a canvas or SVG document model with a small keyboard plumbing input, its own caret/selection/undo logic, a separate formatter, and a differently routed server-backed library. Public ui.md:3 and the custom-surface gate:23 explicitly permit those implementations; render gate:23 discovers controls by purpose, and shared-record gate:32 accepts a successful write without requiring echoed fields. No trivial or conforming false-fail counterexample was found for this assigned check. This is a source-level product-scope assessment; no app judge or Oracle score is claimed. raw-evidence-index.json was absent when checked, so no runtime artifact or artifact hash is cited as measurement evidence; runtime clearance belongs to the separately assigned runtime rows.
